sk-5d908eec.stem: A 22-year-old man who fell on his outstretched hand has tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox; the first X-rays are normal. Two weeks later the fracture line becomes visible. What is the most feared complication of a fracture of this bone?
options: Avascular necrosis of the proximal fragment
Avascular necrosis of the distal fragment
sk-5d908eec.explanation: The scaphoid is the most commonly fractured carpal bone. Its nutrient vessels mostly enter distally, so in waist fractures the blood supply to the proximal fragment is disrupted and avascular necrosis and non-union may follow. The floor of the snuffbox contains the scaphoid and trapezium.

sk-93bbc372.stem: Which carpal bone dislocates most often, and which nerve can it compress when it displaces forwards?
sk-93bbc372.explanation: The lunate can dislocate volarly into the carpal tunnel and compress the median nerve. Avascular necrosis of the lunate is known as Kienböck's disease.

sk-cd43228f.stem: The pisiform is a sesamoid bone that develops within the tendon of which muscle?
sk-cd43228f.explanation: The pisiform lies within the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris and articulates with the triquetrum. Through the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments it transmits the muscle's pull to the hamate and 5th metacarpal; abductor digiti minimi arises from it.

sk-b5971216.stem: A golfer whose club struck the ground has pain in the hypothenar region, numbness of the 4th–5th fingers and weakness spreading and closing the fingers. Which bony process is fractured?
sk-b5971216.explanation: The hook of the hamate forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal (ulnar canal). When it fractures, the ulnar nerve and artery in the canal can be affected, with numbness of the palmar surface of the 4th–5th fingers and weakness of the interossei.

sk-a1b84851.stem: With which metacarpal does the trapezium form a saddle joint?
sk-a1b84851.explanation: The carpometacarpal joint of the thumb (trapezium–1st metacarpal) is a saddle joint; it allows a wide range of movement including opposition and is a common site of osteoarthritis in later life.

sk-341b60e9.stem: Which is the largest carpal bone and the first to ossify?
sk-341b60e9.explanation: The capitate is the largest carpal bone and usually the first to ossify, in the first year. It articulates with the 3rd metacarpal; the axis of wrist movement mostly passes through its head.

sk-ac91683a.stem: A young man who punched a wall has lost the knuckle of his little finger. What is the most likely fracture?
options: Fracture of the hook of the hamate
Fracture of the neck of the 5th metacarpal (boxer's fracture)
Fracture of the base of the 1st metacarpal (Bennett fracture)
Fracture of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
sk-ac91683a.explanation: Punching a hard surface with a closed fist most often fractures the neck of the 5th metacarpal; the head tilts palmarly and the knuckle disappears. A Bennett fracture is an intra-articular fracture of the base of the 1st metacarpal.

sk-31d8147a.stem: What is the order of the proximal row of carpal bones from lateral (radial) to medial (ulnar)?
sk-31d8147a.explanation: Proximal row: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform. Distal row: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate. The radiocarpal joint is formed by the radius and disc with the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum.

sk-9d63d002.stem: Where do the three bones that form the hip bone meet?
sk-9d63d002.explanation: The ilium, ischium and pubis fuse at puberty in the Y-shaped cartilage of the acetabulum. About 2/5 of the acetabulum is formed by the ilium, 2/5 by the ischium and 1/5 by the pubis.

sk-592e9cb4.stem: Which structures pass through the obturator canal?
options: Pudendal nerve and internal pudendal artery
Sciatic nerve and inferior gluteal artery
sk-592e9cb4.explanation: The obturator foramen is closed by the obturator membrane, leaving only the obturator canal at its top. Through it the obturator nerve, artery and vein pass to the medial compartment of the thigh.

sk-ffa0581d.stem: Which nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen?
sk-ffa0581d.explanation: The pudendal nerve, internal pudendal artery and nerve to obturator internus leave through the greater sciatic foramen, wind around the ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament and enter the ischio-anal fossa and Alcock's canal through the lesser sciatic foramen. The ischial spine guides a pudendal block.

sk-602b0bd7.stem: A 78-year-old woman who fell at home has a shortened, externally rotated right leg. X-ray shows a subcapital femoral neck fracture. Damage to which artery is chiefly responsible for avascular necrosis of the femoral head in this fracture?
options: Artery of the ligament of the head of the femur
sk-602b0bd7.explanation: The femoral head is mainly supplied by the retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery ascending along the neck. These vessels are torn in the fracture. The artery in the ligament of the head (from the obturator artery) is insufficient in adults.

sk-b5309bbc.stem: Which muscle attaches to the lesser trochanter?
sk-b5309bbc.explanation: Psoas major and iliacus attach by a common tendon to the lesser trochanter and form the strongest flexor of the hip. Gluteus medius/minimus and piriformis attach to the greater trochanter, obturator externus to the trochanteric fossa.

sk-c857e576.stem: A young woman says her kneecap slipped outwards after twisting her knee playing volleyball. What is the most important dynamic restraint against lateral dislocation of the patella?
sk-c857e576.explanation: The angle between the line of pull of quadriceps and the patellar ligament (Q angle) tends to pull the patella laterally. The lower horizontal fibres of vastus medialis pull it medially; the prominent lateral femoral condyle also forms a bony barrier.
